<user>
Return the next passage of fiction.

I take a short break in the common room. If Seraphel is there and not occupied in a conversation, I ask, "What do you like reading for pleasure?" Otherwise I sit with my book.
</user>

summary: **Positioning Rowan in common room near card game**

item.text:
You mark your place, close the blue volume, and carry it into the common room.

Seraphel is not there. Through the open library doorway, her loose pages remain spread across the upper gallery, and the faint scratch of her pencil continues overhead. Caelindra is still concealed in the west alcove.

The card game occupies a low table near the fireplace. Dena has propped her splinted wrist on a cushion while she plays with her other hand. Thessaly sits beside her, captured cards arranged in exact rows. Rashid and the two visiting students fill out the table.

Rashid acknowledges you with a nod but doesn’t draw you into the game. The half-hour he promised Dena has passed, yet he remains for another deal.

Their conversation has moved well away from injuries and practice groups. Dena is recounting the time Rashid gave a Commerce instructor a brass ruler for Midwinter.

“He used it to measure our assignment margins,” she says. “Then deducted marks from everyone whose lines were an eighth-inch too wide.”

“I was seventeen,” Rashid says. “The gift was sincere.”

“That made it funnier.”

Thessaly studies him across her cards. “You supplied the instrument of your own punishment.”

“Yes.”

She considers this, then plays a card that makes Dena laugh and costs Rashid most of his counters.

You settle into a deep leather chair at the edge of the firelight, the Council book resting closed across your knees. The room asks nothing of you. For several minutes there is only the warmth of the hearth, the soft slap of cards, and conversation continuing comfortably without your management.
